column1: # Game profile of Advance Wars 1+2: Re-Boot Camp (Switch, base game v0 = 1.0.0, the only version). Plays on the Mac and on the iPhone
# Unity 2020.2.1f3 IL2CPP on SDK 10.4.1 (the sdk and movie module builds of The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles), NVN, FMOD (sound through AudioOut), Bink 2 movies (.bk2) decoded by Bink's own
# Unity plugin in main, Pia / NEX for online play. Everything is in Addressables bundles under Data/StreamingAssets/aa/Switch, read as Engage's (unityfs.py).
# Shaders: 20,392 from the bundles and Unity's 11 GLSLC outputs in main, and the Bink plugin's 32 (2 vertex, 22 pixel, 8 compute), whose control sections and code areas lie loose in main
# (shader_split.py raw_shaders); without them the opening movie and every other movie drew white

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk (subsdk0 = NintendoSDK_movie, which main imports from; the movies seen so far, the opening among them, are Bink's)
# The NPDM declares 16 MB of system resource (virtual address memory): nninitStartup (main+0x365310) hands pool − used to StandardAllocator as one address region, and main sets no heap;
# Unity reserves its own regions beside it. Engage's 5 GB block (4.375 GB alias region), with the SDK's address-region node area cut and regions of 1 GB and more aligned to 32 MB on the
# SDK 10.4.1 sdk build (dm/tools/sdk_patches.py). The NSP script's heap check (the hardware pool used the alias region up to +4.25 GB within seconds) set a 1 GB pool, as for the other
# Unity games with virtual address memory, but this game's malloc then failed at the first loading screen: Unity's GPU pool allocation (main+0x96f430) halves its request after each failed
# aligned_alloc down to a size of 0 and spins there for good (frames stopped 17 s in). With 2 GB: 2.26 GB of the alias region mapped and its high-water mark +3.27 GB through 15 minutes of
# the title, the opening movie, the menus and the first training battle; the process holds about 2.5 GB on the Mac, 1.6–1.9 GB of it Metal allocations
# The map cursor moves with the D-pad (the tutorial battle was played with it on the Mac); the 3D layout has one
